numerical_failure.observed_behavior: With use_distance=True, linear_rainbow ordered observations by Mahalanobis distance to the middle-indexed observation exog[nobs // 2] and built the covariance around that single point, so the F-statistic and p-value depended on the raw row order of the data (continuous data: different F across permutations; discrete lattice with ties: 69 distinct F values, spread 0.17 under argsort). With a constant column in exog the covariance was singular and raised a LinAlgError for the typical regression model.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Mahalanobis distances should be measured from the exog centroid (multivariate mean), so the statistic is invariant to row order: spread about 1e-15 (floating-point noise) across permutations, and 1 distinct F for 100 permutations of the discrete lattice. Constant-column model should run without raising, giving F=1.3847543113 with spread 2.2e-16. Ordering uses a deterministic lexsort keyed on distance then exog values, and pseudo-inverse of the covariance handles rank deficiency.
trigger_conditions: data supplied in different row orders (permutations of the observations)
discrete or duplicated regressors causing exact Mahalanobis distance ties under argsort
exog contains a constant column (singular covariance) which raised LinAlgError

input_output_examples.input: continuous data, 5 permutations of rows, use_distance=True

numerical_characteristics.precision: Spread values of 8.9e-16, 2.2e-16 and 6.7e-16 are reported as floating-point noise for continuous, constant-column and discrete-lattice cases; argsort baseline spread 0.17 across 69 distinct F values
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: F-statistic approximately 1.3847543113 in the constant-column model; spreads on the order of 1e-16 to 1e-15 versus 0.17 before the fix
category_specific_evidence: Original bug: linear_rainbow with use_distance=True ordered observations by Mahalanobis distance to exog[nobs // 2], so the same data in a different row order gave a different F-statistic and p-value.
Covariance built around a single middle-indexed observation was singular with a constant exog column, raising LinAlgError.
Fix: center at the exog centroid (multivariate mean), use pseudo-inverse of covariance, and order by deterministic lexsort on distance (primary) and exog values (tie-break) instead of argsort.

Reproducer: continuous data over 5 permutations gave spread 8.9e-16; discrete integer lattice over 100 permutations gave 1 distinct F with spread 6.7e-16, versus 69 distinct values with spread 0.17 under argsort.
Constant-column model no longer raises and gives F=1.3847543113 with spread 2.2e-16.
Invariance property: statistic should be identical across row permutations, since the centroid is order invariant.
Tests named test_rainbow_use_distance_order_invariant and test_rainbow_use_distance_order_invariant_discrete fail on main; test suite reports 138 passed after fix.
reproduction_risks: Discrete lattice case needs exact distance ties to trigger the argsort order dependence; a continuous-only reproducer will not expose the tie-break issue.
The constant-column case is the one that exercised the former LinAlgError.
Passages do not state a tolerance for assert_allclose comparisons; any tolerance must be chosen by the reproducer, not taken from the passages.
The docstring-versus-warning mismatch for center is a separate documentation point and not part of the numerical property.
